author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Unvalidated-input boundary closed: the `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page` on GET /owners is normalized once with `Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)` before any use, and both downstream call sites (`findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` and `addPaginationModel`) consume the normalized `currentPage`. No path in processFindForm reads the raw `page` after the clamp.

Integer-overflow path closed: `page = Integer.MIN_VALUE` previously reached `PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...)`, wrapping to Integer.MAX_VALUE and yielding a silent empty result; the clamp raises it to 1 so the subtraction can no longer underflow. The upper end is unaffected — `Integer.MAX_VALUE` still yields `PageRequest.of(MAX_VALUE-1, 5)` whose offset is computed in long, produces an empty page, and is handled by the existing `ownersResults.isEmpty()` branch rather than an exception.

Fail-open direction is safe: clamping widens the response only to the first page of data the caller could already retrieve with `/owners` (default page 1). No authorization boundary is crossed, and no record becomes reachable that was not already public on this unauthenticated route (docs/system-design.md Security Context).

SQL injection: the paged query stays on the Spring Data derived method `findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable)`; the diff adds no string-concatenated SQL or JPQL. Page number reaches the database only as a bound LIMIT/OFFSET via Pageable.

Output escaping: the only new model value is the int `currentPage`; swept `src/main/resources/templates/` for `th:utext`/`th:inline`/unescaped output and found none, so Thymeleaf default escaping still covers every rendered attribute (matches the XSS row of the Threat Model).

Information disclosure reduced: page values below 1 previously raised IllegalArgumentException from PageRequest.of and rendered the error page; the clamp removes that error path for the whole below-one range.
No secrets introduced: the diff adds one constant (`FIRST_PAGE = 1`), a comment, and tests — swept for token/password/secret/key/credential patterns with no hits.
Supply chain unchanged: the change set is two source files; `build.gradle` and all plugin/dependency versions (Spring Boot 4.1.0) are untouched, so no new dependency surface to verify.

Tests exercise the security-relevant boundary values directly (0, -1, Integer.MIN_VALUE) and assert the resolved Pageable page number rather than only the HTTP status, so a regression in the clamp fails loudly.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice pins a cross-feature commitment durable memory did not carry: the disposition of an out-of-range paging parameter at the web boundary. security-principles.md's Trust Boundaries row establishes that arriving input is range-checked at the boundary but states refusal as the disposition; this slice defines the below-first range as meaningful and answers it with the first page instead. That reading is defensible — the contract now admits the range rather than the boundary letting it through un-ranged — but it is not derivable from durable memory, so it is recorded rather than left to the next reader to re-derive. New ADR 2026-08-05-out-of-range-page-requests-are-normalized.md carries the why; a new system-design.md subsection 'Paged listing routes' under Contracts carries the current state, alongside a new Threat Model row. The one-line clamp and the FIRST_PAGE constant stay local details and are deliberately not documented — consistent with the Constants section's existing exclusion of per-controller page-size and view-name constants.
integration_points: Contracts section gains a 'Paged listing routes' subsection recording that owner search normalizes at the boundary and the veterinarian directory does not
Threat Model gains an 'Out-of-range paging parameter' row; mitigation reads 'none observed' for the vet route, matching the section's existing convention for unmitigated surface
No change to the Contracts table rows for OwnerController or VetController — their purposes are unaltered

patterns.description: Normalize a reader-supplied paging parameter once at the controller boundary, before any use, so a single normalized value feeds both the repository query and the view model. The placement is the load-bearing part: a second normalization further in, or one call site reading the raw value while another reads the normalized one, is the failure this shape prevents.

risks.risk: VetController.showVetList carries the identical unguarded PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) shape. /vets.html?page=0 fails the request; a value far enough below the first wraps through integer arithmetic to a high page and renders an empty table. The two paged routes therefore answer the same input differently.
risks.mitigation: Recorded as current state in system-design.md 'Paged listing routes' and named in the ADR's Implementation and Consequences, so the gap is legible without expanding this slice. Deliberately NOT raised as a code change here — the prd-entry lists the veterinarian directory's paging as a non-goal. Closing it is a product call and wants its own prd-entry against REQ-VET-001; this triage does not open one, because a second route diverging from a just-recorded rule is a documented gap, not a blocker on this slice.

risks.risk: The URL contract is now hard to reverse: answering these requests with a client error later breaks anything holding such a link.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in the ADR's Consequences so a future proposal to refuse meets the prior decision rather than treating the current behavior as incidental.

risks.risk: The design record could be read as settling the whole out-of-range question, including a page above the last.
risks.mitigation: Both the ADR and the system-design subsection state explicitly that only the below-first range is decided, matching the prd-entry's non-goal.

notes: Verdict is 'new' rather than 'covered' on one test: would a competent implementer facing the vet route tomorrow derive this answer from existing memory? No — security-principles.md's boundary row reads as 'reject', so they would plausibly return a client error, leaving the application with two dispositions for one input class. That is the emergent-property failure the design record exists to prevent, and it is what justifies the ADR: hard to reverse (public URL contract), surprising without context (reads against the brief's default disposition), and a real trade-off (a forgiving URL versus surfacing a caller's paging bug). No 'conflicting' verdict: the security brief states a control, not a disposition, and the contract that defines what is allowed is the PRD's — now explicit at edge case 4. No source change is in scope and none is recommended; all code paths listed are already in their approved final state this round (lines 21-23). Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log, silent skip. Basis for the coverage claims is grep over src/main (two @RequestParam sites in the whole application, both paging) plus direct reads of both controllers — the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker, text-level basis.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Normalize-instead-of-refuse is defensible for this input class at this boundary. The trust-boundary rule in security-principles.md states 'Validate type, range, and shape before use; reject what the contract does not allow' — the disposition is conditioned on the contract, not fixed to refusal. The slice moves the contract (prd.md Owner records edge case 4) to admit the below-first range with a defined meaning, so range is still established at the boundary and nothing un-ranged reaches the query. The ADR's reading that refusal is a disposition read into the rule rather than stated by it is correct.

The classic normalization hazard — canonicalize-then-reuse-the-raw-value, or normalize twice at different depths — is absent. Math.max runs once in processFindForm before any use, and currentPage is the only value flowing to findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and to the currentPage model attribute. The Javadoc on findPaginatedForOwnersLastName states the already-normalized precondition, so the internal contract past the boundary is explicit.

The page parameter carries no security decision: it selects no resource path, composes no query text, and gates no authorization (there is none). Its only sink is PageRequest.of on a public unauthenticated read. Normalization is therefore a usability disposition, not a weakened control.

The change is strictly stronger than the baseline in system-design.md § Security Context. It removes an unhandled IllegalArgumentException path that rendered the error page (which echoes the underlying exception message) and closes the Integer.MIN_VALUE underflow that wrapped page-1 to Integer.MAX_VALUE and served an arbitrary high page. No new attack surface, no new endpoint, no new dependency, no credential, no escaping change.

The Out-of-range paging parameter Threat Model row states the residual risk accurately. Verified against VetController: page=0 gives PageRequest.of(-1,5) which throws, and page=Integer.MIN_VALUE overflows to Integer.MAX_VALUE and renders an empty table — exactly the vector text. VetController has no guard, so 'none observed' is the correct mitigation verdict under the section's provenance note. The row scopes itself to the below-first range and does not overclaim above-last coverage; for owner search a high page falls through the existing empty-result branch without an exception, so there is no unstated residual there either.

The unguarded vet route is pre-existing surface the slice did not touch, which under security-principles.md § Applying this section is never a finding — recording it as unresolved current state in system-design.md § Paged listing routes plus the ADR Consequences is the right disposition rather than a silent omission.
No secrets in the diff: the only new constant is FIRST_PAGE = 1, and the @RequestParam defaultValue is a compile-time constant expression over it.
